correctness.rationale: For t>=2 and every m_i>=2, fixing the hub label splits admissible OIDRDFs into four disjoint exhaustive classes; each blade is independently classified by its zero count and minimum defender requirements. The h=0 case correctly uses two independent blades to defend the hub. The resulting product polynomial gives all coefficients; the minima and second coefficient follow from its precisely determined lowest two terms. An independent exhaustive original-predicate checker matched complete weight histograms and minimum/next-weight counts for 16 size vectors, including heterogeneous sizes and up to 10 vertices. Finite checks only corroborate the parameter-uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The surviving assessed novelty is the full weight enumerator for all OIDRDFs on arbitrary heterogeneous one-hub clique bouquets plus its second-weight coefficient. A 2019 corona minimization theorem was found to cover the same graphs and imply the scalar minimum; the scalar and canonical optimum construction are explicitly credited as previously implied, not as new. Searches and inspected relevant full texts revealed no dominating all-weight enumeration, subject to the documented inaccessible original paper and unindexed-priority risks.
residual_risks: The introductory Applied Mathematics and Computation paper DOI:10.1016/j.amc.2019.124617 was not available in full; abstract-only evidence cannot rule out an unstated all-labeling table or construction.
No exhaustive index of publications or databases exists in these checks; differently named weight-partition functions or unindexed literature may subsume the formula.
The exact minimum is a prior-implied corollary of the 2019 general corona theorem, not an originality claim here.

value.rationale: An exact weight distribution on the full heterogeneous blade-size vector gives the number of admissible four-level protection assignments for every resource budget in a natural connected block-graph family, not just a minimum weight. The second coefficient detects a real two-blade boundary: hub labels 0 and 2 become viable one unit above optimum only when there are exactly two blades. The formula specializes simultaneously to friendship and generalized windmill graphs and is a complete self-contained classification, not a handpicked numerical example.
